question: Politicisation of the allocation of EU funding can lead to an unfair distribution of resources, favouring certain groups or regions based on their political affiliations to the detriment of real needs and objective criteria. The risks associated with this include the erosion of public trust in EU and national institutions, inefficient use of EU funds and the slowing of economic and social progress.

In the period 2021-2027, the European Regional Development Funds available to Alba County are being managed by the Centre Regional Development Agency (ADR Centru) as the Managing Authority (MA) for the Centre Region Programme (PR Centru).

The Director-General of ADR Centru has been in his post since 2005, while also holding the post of First Vice-President of the National Liberal Party (PNL) in Alba County and of acting President of the PNL in Alba Iulia municipality. Given these circumstances: 1.

Has the Commission assessed, as part of the MA accreditation process, or independently of this, any political incompatibilities or conflicts of interest as regards the management of the Centre Regional Development Agency?
What measures has the Commission taken to ensure there is no risk of politicisation as regards allocation of EU funding under the Centre Region Programme?
answer: The allocation of EU funding for the Centru regional programme, as for any other programme, is based on objective criteria (1), in particular the population living in the different administrative-territorial units. The procedures for the selection of operations are based on non-discriminatory, inclusive and transparent criteria to maximise the contribution of the Union funding.

The Commission regularly assesses the effective functioning of the management and control systems established by the Member States through controls and audits, with due attention to avoid conflict of interests’ situations. In this respect, the Commission has zero tolerance towards fraud, conflict of interests and any other illegal behaviours.

The Financial Regulation (2) of the EU has further clarified the issue of conflicts of interests under shared management. It now makes Member States authorities expressly responsible for the prevention, detection and correction of conflicts of interests.

The obligation applies at any level, including at political level, in as much as the actor or person concerned is involved in budget implementation under direct, indirect and shared management, including acts preparatory thereto, audit or control. This aspect is in the scope of any audit of the Commission.

The common audit service of the Directorates General for Regional and Urban Policy and Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion carried out an audit on the Centru regional programme in January 2024. The draft audit report was issued in April 2024.

Its findings are, at the moment, subject to a contradictory procedure with the programme authorities and, as such, confidential until the final audit findings are issued as well as the follow-up procedure is completed.
Emergency Government Ordinance No 156 of 3 September 2020. Art. 61 of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 July 2018.
